verses.text: After Abimelek's time, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, rose up to save Israel. He was from the tribe of Issachar and lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He led Israel as judge for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.
After him came Jair from Gilead, who led Israel as judge for twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons, who rode thirty donkeys. They ruled thirty towns in Gilead, which are still called the Settlements of Jair today.
When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon.

Again the Israelites did evil in the LORD's eyes. They served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites and the Philistines. They left the LORD and no longer served him.
So the LORD became angry with Israel and sold them to the Philistines and the Ammonites.
That year these nations crushed and broke the Israelites. For eighteen years they crushed all the Israelites living east of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin and Ephraim. Israel was in great trouble.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, "We have sinned against you. We have left our God and served the Baals."
The LORD answered, "When the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites and the Philistines,
the Sidonians, the Amalekites and the Maonites crushed you, and you cried to me for help, did I not save you from them?
But you have left me and served other gods, so I will not save you any more.
Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you when you are in trouble!"
But the Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do with us whatever you think best, but please save us now."
Then they got rid of the foreign gods among them and served the LORD. And he could no longer bear to see Israel suffer.
The Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead. The Israelites gathered and camped at Mizpah.
The leaders of the people of Gilead said to each other, "Whoever will begin the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of everyone living in Gilead."
